target.title: fix(feishu): pass timeoutMs through app-registration guarded fetch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Feishu app-registration HTTP went through `fetchWithSsrFGuard` without a top-level `timeoutMs`. Sibling Feishu surfaces (`streaming-card`) already pass `timeoutMs` so undici dispatcher + guarded abort both fire. Registration previously relied only on `AbortSignal.timeout` inside `RequestInit`, which does not configure the guarded-fetch dispatcher hang floor the same way.

A Feishu/Lark accounts peer that accepts TCP but never returns headers could stall onboarding / QR registration longer than intended, especially if `init.signal` is dropped on a future refactor.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wire `timeoutMs` into `fetchFeishuJson` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard`, matching the streaming-card pattern:

- Default floor: exported `FEISHU_APP_REGISTRATION_TIMEOUT_MS` (10s) — keeps the tighter wizard budget (not the 30s `FEISHU_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS` API client default)
- Optional `timeoutMs` on registration fetch options for tests / overrides
- Remove redundant `init.signal` timeouts now owned by the guarded fetch

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** Registration HTTP depended on `RequestInit.signal` alone; guarded-fetch `timeoutMs` / dispatcher hang floor was unset.

**After:** Every registration JSON call installs a 10s guarded `timeoutMs`. Hung accounts endpoints reject with `TimeoutError: request timed out`.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.ts`
- Production caller path: `beginAppRegistration` → `postRegistration` → `fetchFeishuJson` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard`
- Regression: `extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.test.ts`
- ClawSweeper follow-up: non-Vitest standalone runtime proof of the production guarded-fetch call shape, including the full 10s default floor

### Caller-path hang proof (Vitest)

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text
[feishu fetchFeishuJson hang proof] timed_out=true name=TimeoutError elapsed_ms=84 production_timeout_ms=10000
 ✓ |extension-feishu| extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.test.ts > Feishu app registration > times out registration POSTs when accounts never return headers 87ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 12.25s
```

## Real behavior proof

**Commands run:**
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.test.ts --reporter=verbose
PROOF_MODE=short node /tmp/openclaw-feishu-registration-timeout-proof/standalone.mjs
PROOF_MODE=production-floor node /tmp/openclaw-feishu-registration-timeout-proof/standalone.mjs
```

**Before fix:**
`fetchFeishuJson` called `fetchWithSsrFGuard` without `timeoutMs`. Registration relied only on `RequestInit.signal = AbortSignal.timeout(...)`.

**After fix:**
Production registration posts install `timeoutMs` (default `FEISHU_APP_REGISTRATION_TIMEOUT_MS = 10000`) into `fetchWithSsrFGuard`. Against a peer that accepts TCP but never returns headers:

1. Short standalone run (`timeoutMs: 80` stand-in)
2. Production-floor standalone run (`timeoutMs: 10000`)

Source wiring verified in the standalone harness: exported 10s constant, `timeoutMs` forwarded into `fetchWithSsrFGuard`, redundant `init.signal` timeouts removed.

**Evidence after fix (Vitest):**
```text
[feishu fetchFeishuJson hang proof] timed_out=true name=TimeoutError elapsed_ms=84 production_timeout_ms=10000
 ✓ ... > times out registration POSTs when accounts never return headers 87ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 12.25s
```

**Evidence after fix (standalone, non-Vitest, short):**
```text

[standalone] mode=short hang_http_peer=http://127.0.0.1:64997 caller=beginAppRegistration→fetchFeishuJson→fetchWithSsrFGuard timeoutMs=80
[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 80ms (elapsed 94ms) operation=fetchWithSsrFGuard url=https://accounts.feishu.cn/oauth/v1/app/registration
[standalone] timeout_or_error name=TimeoutError message=request timed out elapsed_ms=164 accepted_connections=0
[standalone] RESULT timed_out=true elapsed_ok=true expected_floor_ms=80 production_timeout_ms=10000
```

**Evidence after fix (standalone, non-Vitest, production 10s floor):**

Live Feishu/Lark accounts credentials / QR scan UI; gateway packaging beyond the production `beginAppRegistration` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` path used by onboarding.

target.title: [Bug] Incomplete cleanup of expired pairing authorizations leads to memory growth in node registry
target.body:
### Description
When pairing new nodes, authorization session tokens are tracked in node-registry.ts. If the pairing flow is abandoned or times out, the registration callbacks are not properly cleaned up from event-mapper.ts event emitters. This creates dangling references that prevent the session objects from being garbage-collected.

### Affected Files
- src/acp/pairing/node-registry.ts
- src/acp/pairing/event-mapper.ts

### Proposed Solution
1. Attach pairing event listeners with a single-use hook wrapper or explicitly dispose of them inside a timeout cleanup hook in node-registry.ts.
2. Add test assertions in event-mapper.ts verifying listener counts return to baseline after pairing sessions expire.

target.title: [AI-assisted] fix(openai): prefix instruction-aware embedding queries
target.body:
## Summary

AI-assisted PR.

- Problem: OpenAI-compatible embedding providers passed raw query text to instruction-aware embedding models such as Qwen3, Nomic, and mxbai.
- Why it matters: Raw queries produced lower-quality retrieval for instruction-aware embedding models because query embeddings did not match the model's expected retrieval-query format.
- What changed: OpenAI embeddings now apply model-specific query instruction prefixes for query embeddings, while document batch embeddings remain unchanged.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): No embedding defaults, credentials handling, base URL behavior, document embedding inputs, or non-OpenAI providers were changed.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #
- Related #
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** OpenAI-compatible embedding providers now apply model-specific query instruction prefixes for instruction-aware Qwen3, Nomic, and Mixedbread embedding model families on query embeddings, while document/batch embeddings remain raw.

**Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw development checkout at PR head `65a5ce21910de9a43be7bed4ff1d22ab3f757b4b`, using configured model `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-4B` against an OpenAI-compatible vLLM endpoint on coedo. A local redacting/proof proxy only rewrote the model id for backend compatibility and captured the request bodies emitted by the providers.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Ran `tmp/pr-79702-current-head-proof.mts` from the PR worktree after the current-head rebase. The script exercised both touched provider paths: bundled OpenAI query/document embeddings and generic `openai-compatible` query/document embeddings.

**Evidence after fix:** Copied live terminal/request-capture output from the current-head proof run:

```text
Generated at: 2026-06-02T19:18:56.751Z
```

**Observed result after fix:** Both touched provider paths returned 2560-dimensional vectors from live calls. Query request bodies were prefixed with `Instruct: Given a user query, retrieve relevant memory notes and documents\nQuery:...`; document request bodies stayed raw for the same configured model.

**What was not tested:** Every OpenAI-compatible embedding server and additional instruction-aware model families beyond the covered Qwen3, Nomic, and Mixedbread matchers were not tested.

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Missing detection / guardrail: Unit tests did not verify provider-specific query payloads for instruction-aware models.

target.title: fix(line): cap user profile cache
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an unbounded in-process `userProfileCache` in the LINE send path (`extensions/line/src/send.ts`). Profile lookups are cached for 5 minutes (TTL) but had no entry-count cap, so gateways serving many distinct LINE users accumulate Map entries indefinitely until process restart.

**Concrete scenario:** A LINE gateway processing inbound messages from 10 000 distinct users over several hours caches each `getUserProfile` result. With no size cap, the cache grows without bound.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a 1 024-entry cap via the existing `pruneMapToMaxSize` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime`, matching Slack / Discord / Nextcloud Talk channel caches.

`touchLineUserProfileCache` deletes + sets so Map insertion order refreshes on both write and TTL-valid read hits (same LRU-on-access pattern as `extensions/slack/src/channel-type.ts`). Active users stay under the cap; idle oldest-inserted entries evict first.

No config/env knobs. TTL behavior is unchanged.

## User Impact

**Before:** Long-lived LINE gateways accumulate one `userProfileCache` entry per distinct user indefinitely.

**After:** Cache stays at ≤ 1 024 entries. Recently touched profiles survive eviction; untouched oldest entries are pruned. First 1 024 distinct users behave as before until the cap is exceeded.

## Evidence

- `extensions/line/src/send.ts` — `LINE_USER_PROFILE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 1024`, `touchLineUserProfileCache` (delete + set + `pruneMapToMaxSize`) on write and TTL hit

- Sibling pattern: `extensions/slack/src/channel-type.ts` (`getCachedSlackConversationInfo` / `setCachedSlackConversationInfo`)
- Shared helper: `src/infra/map-size.ts` via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime` (`pruneMapToMaxSize`)

target.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A post-turn context-engine **deferred turn maintenance** run can wedge (for example on plugin lock contention) with **no per-task timeout below the ~360s session-level abort**. While it is wedged it holds its maintenance lane, so a user message queued behind it on the same session can wait minutes before being processed, even though the model is healthy. `session.stalled` also re-warns on every ~30s heartbeat with no backoff, spamming the logs.

This matches the report in #96703: an interactive session effectively hangs until a manual stop.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three concrete gaps in core code (independent of any specific context-engine plugin):

1. **No per-task timeout was available on the maintenance enqueue.** `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance` enqueued the maintenance worker via `enqueueCommandInLane(...)` with no options. The command queue already supports a per-task timeout (`taskTimeoutMs` → rejects with `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` and releases the lane), but the maintenance lane never wired it up, so an operator hitting the wedge had no knob below the session-level abort.
2. **A timed-out maintenance worker was not fenced.** Rejecting the enqueue promise releases the lane, but it does not stop the still-running worker. A wedged worker could later call `runtimeContext.rewriteTranscriptEntries()` or complete/fail the task **after** the active run was cleared and a queued foreground turn proceeded, breaking the same-session wait-before-read invariant.
3. **`session.stalled` had no log backoff.** `session.stuck` and `session.long_running` already throttle repeats; `session.stalled` did not.

This change adds the bound + fence mechanism and ships it **opt-in / disabled by default**, so existing deployments whose background maintenance legitimately runs longer than a couple of minutes are not force-cancelled on upgrade. An operator hitting the wedge sets the new key to a positive millisecond value to arm it.

## User Impact

- **No behavior change on upgrade unless configured.** The per-task timeout is **disabled by default** — background turn maintenance keeps running unbounded exactly as before. There is no new force-cancel of long-running background engines on upgrade.
- Operators experiencing the wedge **opt in** by setting `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` to a positive millisecond value (absent or `0` keeps it disabled). When set, a wedged run is bounded at that value and the lane is released, so a queued user message proceeds at ~the timeout instead of waiting for the session-level abort.
- When the bound is armed and fires, late maintenance side effects are **fenced**: the runtime-owned `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper and the worker's terminal complete/fail/descriptor writes become no-ops, so a non-cooperative plugin cannot corrupt session state after the foreground turn has resumed. When the bound is disabled, the fence is never armed.
- A persistently stalled session no longer floods the logs; the first `session.stalled` warning is immediate, repeats are throttled, and recovery is never gated by the backoff.

### Changes

- `command-queue`: add an optional `onTaskTimeout` hook fired synchronously when the per-task timeout rejects, before the lane is released.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: resolve an **opt-in** per-task timeout from `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` (absent / `0` / non-positive ⇒ no bound, no fence); when a positive value is set, pass `taskTimeoutMs` + `onTaskTimeout` to the deferred maintenance enqueue and trip a per-run fence on timeout (hook + defensive trip in the timeout catch); thread the fence into the worker and the runtime-context `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper (checked at entry, inside the session-manager rewrite lock, and before the runtime-transcript write) and before the worker's `completeTaskRunByRunId` / `failTaskRunByRunId` / progress writes.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: scope the timeout classification to the resolved maintenance lane — only this deferred lane's `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` trips the timeout/fence path; a foreign-lane queue timeout surfacing on the enqueue falls through to the normal schedule-failure path (the lane is computed once and reused for enqueue + classification so they cannot drift).
- `session.stalled`: apply the existing `session.stuck`/`session.long_running` warn backoff (`max(last + threshold, last * 2)`), first emission immediate, recovery never gated.
- Config schema accepts `0` (`nonnegative`) as the explicit "disable" sentinel; help/types/docs document the opt-in default.
- New unit coverage: queue `onTaskTimeout` hook; timeout disabled by default and when set to `0`; configured bound + fence arming; late rewrite fenced after timeout; timed-out task not resurrected to succeeded/failed; checkpoint-after-timeout ordering; `session.stalled` backoff.

## Evidence

AI-assisted PR (implemented with an AI coding agent; author reviewed and understands the change).

**Static / unit validation** (this branch):
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:test:src` — clean
- `command-queue.test.ts` — 34 passed; `context-engine-maintenance.test.ts` — 60 passed (incl. disabled-by-default, `0`-disables, and fence cases)
- `oxfmt --check` + oxlint on touched files — clean
- `CHANGELOG.md` not touched (left for maintainers at landing)

**Real runtime reproduction (end-to-end, in a container).** A real gateway was started in a container running this branch, with a real context-engine plugin selected via `plugins.slots.contextEngine` whose `info.turnMaintenanceMode = "background"` (so a normal `reason:"turn"` run is deferred through `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance`). Its `maintain()` deliberately sleeps 12s (longer than the configured timeout) and then attempts a late transcript rewrite. The bound was **explicitly opted in** for the test: `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs = 5000`. Two real agent turns were run on one session. Everything in the queue/timeout/fence/transcript-rewrite path is real production code; only the plugin's deliberate sleep is contrived. Logs redacted (provider/model/host/ids replaced with placeholders):

```
[T+0.00s] [context-engine] deferred turn maintenance queued taskId=<id-1> sessionKey=<session> lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session>
[T+0.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 START                       # deferred maintenance begins, will sleep 12s
[T+2.87s] (queued) second turn is waiting behind the in-flight deferred maintenance on the session lane
[T+5.00s] [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session> durationMs=5000 error="CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError: ... task timed out after 5000ms"
[T+5.00s] [agent/embedded] deferred context engine maintenance timed out: sessionKey=<session> taskId=<id-1> taskTimeoutMs=5000
[T+5.06s] [agent/embedded] embedded run start: <turn-2>   # queued turn RELEASED at the 5s timeout — NOT after the 12s wedge, NOT after the ~360s session abort
[T+12.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 WOKE after 12000ms sleep, attempting late rewrite   # the wedged worker finally wakes, 7s after the lane was released
[T+12.01s] [wedge] maintain#1 late rewrite result: {"changed":false,"bytesFreed":0,"rewrittenEntries":0,"reason":"maintenance fenced after timeout"}   # FENCED -> no-op
```

Fence scope is correct: the second turn's **foreground** maintenance (not timed out) is **not** fenced (`reason: "no replacements requested"`); only the timed-out **deferred** runs are fenced. With the bound left at its default (disabled), neither the timeout nor the fence arms and background maintenance runs unbounded as before. A scripted reproduction is available on request.

Closes #96703

target.title: fix(exec-approvals): handle same-process sync/async lock contention
target.body:
## Problem

The exec-approvals store uses two lock mechanisms sharing the same `.lock` file:

1. **Async sidecar lock** (via `@openclaw/fs-safe`): Used by `resolveExecApprovalsLocked`, `updateExecApprovals`, `loadExecApprovalsAsync`. Has `allowReentrant: true`.

2. **Sync custom lock** (`acquireExecApprovalsLockSync`): Used by `loadExecApprovals`, `readExecApprovalsSnapshot`, `resolveExecApprovals`.

When the async lock holds the `.lock` file (e.g., during `ensureExecApprovalsSnapshot`), the sync lock attempts fail immediately because `acquireExecApprovalsLockSync` detects `ownerPid === process.pid` and treats it as self-deadlock — it does not retry. The failure triggers `createFailClosedExecApprovalsFallback()` → `security: "deny"`. All subsequent execs see `security=deny` and are denied.

The key condition in `acquireExecApprovalsLockSync`:
```typescript
if (state.ownerPid !== null && state.ownerPid !== process.pid && attempt < RETRIES) {
    sleepExecApprovalsSyncLockRetry();
    continue;
}
throw error; // Falls through for same-PID → immediate fail
```

## Fix

Added `isExecApprovalsProcessLocalLockContention()` to detect this specific scenario: `file_lock_timeout` error where the lock is owned by the current process and the target file already exists.

Modified `withExecApprovalsReadLockSync()` to catch same-process contention in both code paths and fall back to lockless reads.

### Why this is safe

- Async writes use atomic temp-file + rename → concurrent reads always see a consistent snapshot
- Only applies to **read** locks — write serialization is preserved
- Lockless fallback only triggers when the **target file already exists**, preserving fail-closed behavior during initial policy creation (no file yet → writer must not be bypassed)

## Changes

- `src/infra/exec-approvals.ts`: Added `isExecApprovalsProcessLocalLockContention()` helper + modified `withExecApprovalsReadLockSync()` (both code paths)
- `src/infra/exec-approvals-store.test.ts`: Added test that simulates same-process lock contention and verifies `loadExecApprovals()` and `readExecApprovalsSnapshot()` return real policy instead of fail-closed deny

## Testing

All 72 exec-approvals store tests pass, including the new test and the existing "fails closed when a writer locks the store before creating the policy file" test (which verifies the fail-closed path is preserved when the target file doesn't exist).

Closes #106777

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Same-process sync/async lock contention in exec-approvals causes all exec commands to be denied with security=deny when the async sidecar lock is held during synchronous policy reads (issue #106777).

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node.js v24.16.0, OpenClaw gateway running locally with single-process mode.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```
cd /mnt/data/repos/forks/openclaw
npx vitest run src/infra/exec-approvals-store.test.ts --no-coverage
```

**Evidence after fix**:
```
RUN  v4.1.9 /mnt/data/repos/forks/openclaw

 ✓  infra  ../../src/infra/exec-approvals-store.test.ts (72 tests) 435ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  72 passed (72)
   Start at  20:21:35
   Duration  911ms (transform 332ms, setup 231ms, import 122ms, tests 435ms, environment 0ms)
```

**Observed result after fix**: All 72 tests pass including the new same-process lock contention test (verifies loadExecApprovals and readExecApprovalsSnapshot return real policy instead of fail-closed deny) and the existing fail-closed test (verifies deny when target file does not exist). The lockless read fallback correctly activates only for same-PID contention when the policy file already exists.

**What was not tested**: Multi-process lock contention across separate gateway instances (requires Docker or multi-node setup). Windows-specific file locking behavior. Production gateway with high-frequency concurrent exec calls.

target.title: fix(voice-call): reject malformed Telnyx timestamps
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telnyx voice webhook verification could accept a signed `telnyx-timestamp` header with trailing non-numeric characters. A header such as `<current-unix-seconds>abc` is still part of the signed `timestamp|payload` string, but the previous verifier truncated it with `Number.parseInt(...)` before applying the replay-window check.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telnyx webhook signing treats the timestamp header as the signed timestamp string, and the OpenClaw verifier documents that header as Unix seconds. This change keeps signature verification over the original header value, but only converts it to an event time when the entire header is an unsigned base-10 Unix-seconds token.

## User Impact

Voice-call users with Telnyx webhooks now get stricter timestamp validation. Valid Telnyx webhooks continue to verify, while malformed signed timestamp headers are rejected before replay-window evaluation.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(discord): add timeout to guarded gateway metadata fetches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Discord gateway metadata HTTP through `fetchDiscordGatewayMetadataGuarded` could hang in DNS/proxy preflight because the `/gateway/bot` deadline lived only in `init.signal`, while `fetchWithSsrFGuard` aborts preflight from its top-level `signal`. A stalled Discord API / proxy preflight could block gateway startup until process restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper P1: forward the existing `withAbortTimeout` AbortSignal as the guard's top-level `signal`, and keep a single deadline owner:

- When `init.signal` is present (production `/gateway/bot` path): pass `{ signal: callerSignal }` only — no second `timeoutMs` timer
- When unsignaled: install `timeoutMs` hang floor (default 30s / `gatewayInfoTimeoutMs`)
- Thread resolved `gatewayInfoTimeoutMs` through `createDiscordGatewayMetadataFetch` / invalid-proxy fallback for the unsignaled hang floor

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled Discord metadata DNS/proxy preflight ignored the gateway metadata abort signal and could hang forever.

**After:** The same `/gateway/bot` timeout AbortSignal cancels guarded-fetch preflight and fetch. Unsignaled guarded metadata calls still fail closed after the configured hang floor.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-metadata.ts`, `gateway-plugin.ts`
- Regressions: `gateway-metadata.test.ts`, `gateway-plugin.test.ts`
- Production caller: `createDiscordGatewayPlugin` → `fetchDiscordGatewayInfoWithTimeout` → `fetchDiscordGatewayMetadataGuarded` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard`

### Unit + wrapper-level hung-peer / stalled-preflight

```bash

```


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Guarded Discord gateway metadata fetches observe the `/gateway/bot` abort signal during DNS/proxy preflight; unsignaled calls keep a hang floor.
- **Canonical reachability path:** `createDiscordGatewayPlugin` → `fetchDiscordGatewayInfoWithTimeout` (`withAbortTimeout` → `init.signal`) → `fetchDiscordGatewayMetadataGuarded` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard({ signal })`.
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime HTTP; loopback `node:http` peer that accepts TCP without writing headers; stalled DNS preflight via injected `lookupFn` on the real guard while the Discord wrapper owns signal wiring.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused `DEFAULT_DISCORD_GATEWAY_INFO_TIMEOUT_MS` / `resolveDiscordGatewayInfoTimeoutMs` and `fetchWithSsrFGuard` top-level `signal` contract; no new Discord config key.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` + `node --import tsx` standalone hung-peer harness.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash

PROOF_MODE=short node --import tsx /tmp/discord-gateway-metadata-timeout-proof.mjs
```

```text
 ✓ |extension-discord| ... > aborts when the shared guarded fetch times out before headers arrive 261ms
 ✓ |extension-discord| ... > times out hung loopback responses through the production timeout owner path 254ms
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  26 passed (26)
```

- **Evidence after fix (standalone hung peer):**

```text
[standalone] source_signal_forward=true source_no_duplicate_timer=true source_withAbortTimeout_owner=true production_timeout_ms=30000
[standalone] mode=short hang_http_peer=http://127.0.0.1:57918/gateway/bot caller=fetchDiscordGatewayInfoWithTimeout→fetchDiscordGatewayMetadataGuarded→fetchWithSsrFGuard timeoutMs=250
```

target.title: fix(tlon): clear SSE connect timeout after failed openStream
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Tlon Urbit SSE `openStream` armed a 60s connect `setTimeout` and only cleared it after a successful `urbitFetch`. When the connect fetch rejected (DNS/SSRF/network) or returned non-OK, the timer stayed armed until it fired, and reconnect storms could stack dangling timers in the Gateway process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wrap the connect fetch in `try/finally` and always `clearTimeout`, matching the zalouser probe timeout cleanup pattern, so failed connects release the timer immediately without changing the connect deadline or stream lifecycle.

## User Impact

Flaky Urbit hosts no longer leave dangling connect timers in long-running Tlon monitors during reconnect failures.

## Evidence

### Unit regression (mocked fetch + fake timers)

```bash

```

The reject case uses a closed loopback port (`127.0.0.1:9`) so the production transport fails before headers.

- **Canonical reachability path:** Tlon monitor reconnect → `UrbitSSEClient.openStream` → production `urbitFetch` / `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → reject or non-OK → `finally { clearTimeout(timeoutId) }`.
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime HTTP; loopback `node:http` + closed-port TCP failure; production SSRF-guarded transport (no `urbitFetch` mock, no fake timers).

target.title: Fix/OpenAI device code request timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running OpenAI Codex device-code login (`openclaw models auth login --provider openai --device-code`, or the equivalent configure/wizard auth choice) could hang forever when a single `auth.openai.com` HTTP request stopped responding.

Before this patch, the flow enforced a 15-minute poll-loop deadline around authorization waiting, and callers could cancel via `AbortSignal`, but the three HTTP calls for user-code request, authorization poll, and token exchange had no per-request operation deadline covering both headers and body reads. A stalled TCP/proxy/blackhole response, or a server that returned headers and then stalled the body, could leave the CLI spinner stuck.

## Why This Change Was Made

Treat each device-code HTTP call as one timed operation: headers fetch plus bounded body read under `buildOAuthRequestSignal` (caller `AbortSignal` composed with `AbortSignal.timeout`, 30s, aligned with the sibling ChatGPT browser OAuth token request timeout). Poll requests clamp that timeout to the remaining 15-minute authorization deadline and retry only on operation timeout (including post-header body stalls) until the overall deadline expires. Caller cancel (Ctrl-C / wizard abort) remains distinguishable and does not retry. User-code and token-exchange timeouts fail fast with a clear error.

Body/fetch aborts rethrow the composed signal reason so undici `AbortError` collapse does not erase `TimeoutError` vs caller cancel distinguishability.

Scope stays OpenAI Codex device-code login HTTP only; browser OAuth and other providers are unchanged.

## User Impact

**Before:** A hung device-code HTTP request (or a post-header body stall) could block `models auth login --device-code` indefinitely, even past the advertised 15-minute authorization window, while still depending on the overall poll deadline for happy-path waiting.

**After:** Each device-code request+body read aborts after 30 seconds (or sooner near the overall deadline). Poll timeouts retry within the 15-minute window; caller cancel aborts immediately without retry; user-code and token-exchange stalls surface an explicit timeout error instead of hanging forever.

## Evidence

- `extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.ts` — `buildOAuthRequestSignal` composes caller cancel + 30s operation deadline across fetch + body read; poll retries only on operation timeout
- Regression: `extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.test.ts`
  - hung user-code / token-exchange abort with timeout error
  - poll retries after `TimeoutError` and completes
  - caller cancel during hung fetch / poll wait / post-header body stall does not retry or map to timeout
  - real `node:http` partial-body stall coverage
  - success path asserts fetches carry an `AbortSignal`

target.title: fix(policy): reject nondecimal watch interval
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `policy watch --interval-ms` accepted JavaScript-specific coercion forms — leading plus (`+500`), leading zeros (`0500`), or longer zero-padded spellings (`000500`) — silently normalizing them to a different but valid integer before reaching the polling loop. Operators resuming from a documented decimal `intervalMs` could therefore request an unintended cadence through a non-canonical alias the parser still accepted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The watch-interval parser now uses the shared `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/number-runtime` and additionally enforces a decimal-only envelope (trimmed input must equal `String(raw)`) so JS coercion forms are rejected at the CLI boundary. Canonical decimal values, the default of `2000`, and the documented lower bound of `250` continue to route unchanged.

This mirrors the canonical sibling `extensions/google-meet/src/cli.ts` (which uses `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` for `--since`) and the broader Wave 1 strict-parser cohort (#106384, #106926, #105557), and adds the decimal-only envelope because `--interval-ms` is documented as a decimal rather than an opaque cursor.

## User Impact

`policy watch --interval-ms` now only accepts canonical decimal non-negative integers. Plus-prefixed, leading-zero-padded, and non-decimal spellings fail fast with the existing `--interval-ms must be an integer >= 250.` message instead of reaching the polling loop as a different cadence. The default `2000`, the boundary `250`, and every previously accepted documented decimal interval are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Before fix (FAIL on pinned main `7b16b35cb3`)

```text
 FAIL  |extensions| extensions/policy/src/cli.test.ts > policy commands > rejects noncanonical plus-prefixed and leading-zero policy watch intervals before evaluating policy
AssertionError: interval=+500: expected 1 to be 2 // Object.is equality

- Expected: 2
+ Received: 1

  at extensions/policy/src/cli.test.ts:384:45

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 33 passed (34)
```

### After fix (PASS on patched head)

```text
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  34 passed (34)
   Duration  9.86s
```

### Focused regression

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/policy/src/cli.test.ts` — 34/34 passed (33 existing + 1 new `rejects noncanonical plus-prefixed and leading-zero policy watch intervals` covering `+500`, `+250`, `0500`, `000500`).
- `git diff --check` — clean.

### Local CLI smoke deferral

Local Node 22.22.0 is below the required 22.22.3 floor, so the `pnpm openclaw policy watch …` launcher refuses to spawn. The vitest `runPolicyWatchJson({ intervalMs: "+500" })` path exercises the canonical `registerPolicyCli(program)` + `program.parseAsync(["policy", "watch", "--interval-ms", "+500", "--once", "--json"])` end-to-end — same code path the launcher invokes on a supported Node. Hosted Testbox will run the full CLI smoke.

### What was NOT changed

- `openclaw/plugin-sdk/number-runtime` shared helper — left as-is so opaque numeric cursors in other extensions (google-meet `--since`, etc.) keep their permissive `+`/leading-zero coercion.
- Default `2000` and lower bound `250` for `--interval-ms`.
- Existing error message string.
- Config, schema, protocol, plugin SDK, plugin manifest, or runtime hooks.
- Any other `--interval-ms` consumer outside `extensions/policy/src/cli.ts`.

## Risk / Compatibility

🚨 compatibility: `+500`, `0500`, and `000500` were silently accepted as `500` by the old parser; they are now rejected at the CLI boundary. No documented decimal interval (`2000`, `250`, `500`, etc.) is affected. Canonical decimal values continue to route unchanged.

## Follows

- #106384 — `fix(google-meet): reject nondecimal transcript cursors`
- #106926 — `fix(onepassword): validate audit limit strictly`
- #105557 — `fix(cli): reject noncanonical trajectory export requests`

## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI-compatible embedding HTTP calls only forwarded an optional caller `AbortSignal`. Gateway `/v1/embeddings` and capability-CLI paths call `embed` / `embedBatch` without a signal, so a server that accepts the TCP connection but never sends headers could hang the request forever. Memory/wiki callers already install their own deadlines; this gap is the unsignaled transport path.

## Why This Change Was Made

When `signal` is omitted, install operation-specific hang bounds via existing `fetchWithSsrFGuard` `timeoutMs`:

- `embed` (query): 60s — aligned with memory remote query defaults
- `embedBatch` (batch): 120s — aligned with memory remote batch defaults so gateway/CLI batches are not clamped below established batch policy

When a caller already provides a signal, leave that deadline alone so memory search / tool timeouts are not clamped.

No new config surface. Test-only override shortens the floor for hang repros.

## User Impact

**Before:** Unsignaled openai-compatible embedding requests (gateway HTTP embeddings, capability CLI) could hang indefinitely on a stalled upstream.

**After:** Unsignaled query requests fail after 60s; unsignaled batch requests fail after 120s (`TimeoutError` / `request timed out`). Callers that pass `AbortSignal` keep their own budget.

target.title: fix(mattermost): bound websocket handshake waits at 30s
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Mattermost's default websocket factory set `maxPayload` but not `handshakeTimeout`. `createMattermostConnectOnce` waits for the `open` event; when a peer accepts TCP but never completes the websocket upgrade, that wait never ends. Slack relay and browser CDP already bound handshake waits at 30s.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Keep a private `buildMattermostWebSocketClientOptions` as the single production options surface (`handshakeTimeout: 30_000`).
- Default Mattermost `WebSocket` factory consumes that builder.
- Regressions observe that production wiring in source (knip-safe; no new unused exports) and prove stalled-handshake timeout returns control to `runWithReconnect`.

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** A Mattermost host that accepted TCP without completing the websocket handshake could pin the channel reconnect loop forever on that attempt.

**After:** Handshake waits fail closed after 30s (`WebSocketClosedBeforeOpenError` / close before open), allowing the reconnect loop to continue.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-websocket.ts`
- Production caller: `createMattermostConnectOnce` / `runWithReconnect` (same path as `monitor.ts`)
- Sibling: `extensions/slack/src/monitor/relay-source.ts` (`handshakeTimeout: 30_000`)

target.title: fix(secrets): collect persona-level TTS provider SecretRefs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Persona-level TTS provider API keys were not collected as SecretRefs and agent persona registry paths bound the wrong path segment as providerId (literal `providers` instead of `elevenlabs`). That breaks secrets plan/audit and runtime resolution for agent persona TTS keys.

Fixes #89607

## Summary

The secret collector walks `messages.tts.providers.*.apiKey` but does not walk `messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` or `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`. When a persona overrides the TTS provider config with a file-source SecretRef, the secret resolver never sees the ref, so the `apiKey` reaches the plugin as an unresolved object instead of the actual key string. The plugin then reports `not configured`.

This fix:
- Adds persona-level provider iteration in `collectTtsApiKeyAssignments`
- Registers two new target paths in the secret target registry (`messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` and `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`)
- Extends `hasAgentRuntimeSecretRefs` to detect persona-level TTS refs
- Adds 5 regression tests covering top-level, persona-level, combined, empty-persona, and agent-level persona paths

Closes #89607

## Evidence

Terminal output from `tsx` against the patched branch showing correct `providerId` binding and persona file SecretRef collection (see Real behavior proof for full capture).

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Agent persona TTS SecretRef paths must resolve `providerId` to the provider key (e.g. `elevenlabs`), not the literal `providers` segment, so plan/audit/runtime metadata match the configured provider. Persona-level file SecretRefs must be collected under `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`.

Closes #106910

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where installed `AgentToolResultMiddleware` handlers on the
OpenClaw embedded runtime never received `agentId`, `sessionId`,
`sessionKey`, or `runId`, even though those fields are part of the public
middleware context and the Codex path already forwards them. Middleware
used for audit, telemetry, or session-scoped policy therefore could not
attribute OpenClaw tool-result events.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildAgentToolResultMiddlewareFactory` constructed
`createAgentToolResultMiddlewareRunner({ runtime: "openclaw" })` only.
Pass agent/session/run identity from the embedded attempt (and compact)
call sites into that runner, matching the Codex `toToolResultHookContext`
shape. Fall back to `SessionManager.getSessionId()` when an explicit
session id is not provided.

## User Impact

Installed middleware that declares OpenClaw runtime support can now see
the same agent/session/run identity fields on OpenClaw tool results that
it already receives on Codex.

## Evidence

```console
$ # Shape before vs after (mirrors factory construction)
BEFORE {"runtime":"openclaw"}
AFTER  {"runtime":"openclaw","agentId":"main","sessionId":"s-explicit","sessionKey":"agent:main:chat","runId":"run-1"}
```

```console
$ pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/extensions.test.ts
 ✓ |agents-core| .../extensions.test.ts (7 tests)
```

- **Real environment tested:** macOS darwin arm64, worktree `/tmp/oc-106910` on `fix/tool-result-middleware-context`, Node via pnpm vitest.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Standalone context construction proof + `pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/extensions.test.ts` and `tool-result-middleware.test.ts`.

- **Observed result after fix:** OpenClaw path matches the public `AgentToolResultMiddlewareContext` fields Codex already provides.

target.title: test(plugins): cover manifest tool-availability gating
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/plugins/manifest-tool-availability.ts` is the gate that decides which plugin-declared tools actually surface to an agent. It resolves manifest **config signals** (root + overlay merge, `required` / `requiredAny`), **auth signals** (provider auth callback, `providerAuthEnvVars` / setup env-var fallback, `SecretRef` env resolution), the **provider base-URL allowlist guard** (which can veto an otherwise-valid auth signal), and the **fail-open contract** (a tool with no manifest metadata must stay available). This module shipped with no direct coverage, so a regression in any of these gates — for example hiding an unannotated tool, or dropping the base-URL allowlist veto that keeps a tool from reaching an off-allowlist proxy — would not be caught before merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change is coverage-only: it adds `src/plugins/manifest-tool-availability.test.ts` (+445, one new file) pinning the module's five exported gates against their current `main` behavior. No production code is touched. Scenarios were chosen to bite on the real failure modes — fail-open flips, base-URL normalization, `requiredAny` value semantics, and the config overlay merge — rather than to chase line count.

**Scope boundary:** no runtime/production file changes, no new config or defaults, no behavior change; the diff is a single new file under `src/plugins/`.

## User Impact

No user-visible or runtime change. For maintainers, the manifest tool-availability gates — a compatibility-sensitive surface per the repo's own review policy — now regress loudly instead of silently: a future edit that breaks the fail-open contract or the base-URL allowlist veto will fail this suite.

## Evidence

Linux (Node 22.22), `pnpm install` from source, rebased onto current `main` (`98ca8c94`). To prove the new scenarios exercise the **real** production gate rather than stubs, a standalone script imports `hasManifestToolAvailability` from the shipped module and drives the eight boundary cases with `node --import tsx`:

```text
$ node --import tsx drive-mta.mts
no config, no auth, no env          => false
config apiKey under webSearch       => true
auth callback grants xai            => true
XAI_API_KEY in env                  => true
whitespace-only XAI_API_KEY         => false
unlisted tool (no metadata)         => true
baseUrl guard, foreign proxy URL    => false
baseUrl guard, trailing slashes     => true
```

Each line is the real return of `hasManifestToolAvailability` for that input: the fail-open `unlisted tool => true`, the whitespace-only env value correctly rejected, and the base-URL guard vetoing a foreign proxy while accepting the allowlisted host after trailing-slash normalization. Reverting the fail-open branch in the module (`return true` → `return false` for the no-metadata case) flips two of these lines, confirming the coverage is non-vacuous.

**Related:** none — coverage mined from the module itself; no linked issue.

target.title: fix(codex): continue after source-reply delivery instead of terminating turn
target.body:
Fixes #106961

## Summary

Codex-backed agent turns prematurely terminated after an intermediate source-reply message send, preventing subsequent tool execution; this fix removes the implicit terminate-on-delivery classification so the turn continues until the normal Codex turn/completed lifecycle.
- Problem: In `message_tool_only` mode, a successful message-tool send to the source channel set `terminate=true` on the dynamic tool response, causing `scheduleTurnReleaseAfterTerminalDynamicTool` to interrupt the turn before subsequent tools could execute.
- Solution: Remove `deliveredSourceReply` and `receiptConfirmedSourceReply` from the `withDynamicToolTermination` conditions; only an explicit `final=true` argument now terminates the turn, matching the generic embedded-runner behavior from PR #92343.
- What changed: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.ts` (terminate classification + sourceReplyFinal telemetry), `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts` (updated assertions + new regression test)
- What did NOT change: `shouldReleaseTurnAfterTerminalDynamicTool`, `resolveTerminalDynamicToolBatchAction`, `shouldBlockTerminalReleaseForNonTerminalDynamicToolResult`, generic embedded-runner suppression logic, finalize path, any config/env/schema surface

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related #106961
- Related #92343 (prior generic fix establishing the desired behavior)
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Issue #106961 reports a Codex-specific recurrence of premature message-tool turn termination on v2026.7.1. The prior generic fix (PR #92343, commit `4620929`) corrected the embedded runner to continue after source-reply delivery, but PR #95942 (commit `9b9a124c`) re-introduced the same termination behavior in the Codex app-server path. Commit `4dc6e182c3` further hardened the incorrect "degrade to terminate-on-delivery when `final` is omitted" logic. This regression breaks Discord/Codex workflows where an agent sends an acknowledgment ("One moment") and then needs to execute further tools.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

**Behavior addressed**: Codex dynamic tool bridge terminates the turn immediately after a successful source-reply message send, preventing subsequent tool calls in the same turn.

**Real environment tested**: Linux, Node v24.13.1, branch `fix/codex-source-reply-terminate-106961`

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
node --experimental-vm-modules node_modules/.bin/vitest run \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose
```

Runs the actual OpenClaw vitest suite against the patched `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` runtime, not a copied classifier. This is the same test file and runtime the CI uses.

**Evidence after fix**:

```console
$ node --experimental-vm-modules node_modules/.bin/vitest run \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose | tail -30

 ✓ |extension-codex| ... > createCodexDynamicToolBridge > does not mark delivered
   message-tool-only source replies as terminal when final is omitted
 ✓ |extension-codex| ... > createCodexDynamicToolBridge > requires explicit
   final=true to make a delivered message-tool-only source reply terminal
 ✓ |extension-codex| ... > createCodexDynamicToolBridge > continues after an
   intermediate message-tool-only source reply without final
 ✓ |extension-codex| ... > createCodexDynamicToolBridge > does not deliver
   message-tool-only source replies as delivered telemetry …
 ✓ |extension-codex| ... > createCodexDynamicToolBridge > does not mark explicit
   message-tool sends as terminal source replies
 ✓ |extension-codex| ... > createCodexDynamicToolBridge > does not mark mismatched
   explicit message-tool sends as terminal source replies
 ✓ |extension-codex| ... > createCodexDynamicToolBridge > records message-tool-owned
   terminal replies as delivered source replies

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  100 passed (100)
```

All 100 tests pass. Key regression test "continues after an intermediate message-tool-only source reply without final" validates the exact #106961 scenario: intermediate message → subsequent exec call → both with terminate=undefined.

**Observed result after fix**:

1. Intermediate message-tool-only source replies (final omitted) no longer set terminate=true
2. sourceReplyFinal telemetry remains true when final is omitted for delivered/receipt source replies — preserves completed marker for stranded-reply recovery (no duplicate replay on error/timeout)
3. Receipt-confirmed source replies (final omitted) no longer set terminate=true
4. Explicit final=true + actual source reply delivery still terminates the turn
5. Cross-channel message-tool sends with final=true do NOT terminate (not a source reply)
6. Tool-returned terminate:true (toolConfirmedSourceReply) still terminates unless overridden by final=false
7. Yield results still terminate correctly
8. didDeliverSourceReplyViaMessageTool and messagingToolSourceReplyPayloads are still correctly collected

**What was not tested**: Live Discord/Codex run with a real Codex-backed agent; requires Crabbox/Testbox + Discord credential. stranding-recovery duplicate protection relies on sourceReplyFinal=true remained consistent — the Completed marker is preserved so recovery will not re-deliver an already-successful message.

## Root Cause

PR #95942 (commit `9b9a124c`) added Codex app-server source-reply support by including `deliveredSourceReply` and `receiptConfirmedSourceReply` in the `withDynamicToolTermination` conditions. This re-introduced the premature termination that PR #92343 (commit `4620929`) had just removed from the generic embedded runner. Commit `4dc6e182c3` further hardened the incorrect "final omitted → degrade to terminate-on-delivery" fallback, making the regression harder to detect.

## Regression Test Plan

- `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts` — covers all source-reply terminate scenarios including the new "continues after an intermediate message-tool-only source reply without final" test
- `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts` — covers shouldReleaseTurnAfterTerminalDynamicTool (unchanged by this fix)
- `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.dynamic-tools.test.ts` — covers terminal diagnostics (unchanged)
- `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/message-tool-terminal.test.ts` — covers generic hook behavior (unchanged)
- `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe*.test.ts` — covers duplicate-output suppression (unchanged)

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Codex-backed Discord agents will no longer stop executing after sending an intermediate acknowledgment message. The agent will continue the turn, executing subsequent tools and delivering the final result, matching the behavior of the generic embedded runner.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — correcting the Codex terminal classification to match the established generic source-reply contract is the narrowest fix that addresses the regression without introducing new surfaces.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: Adding a new config option to control terminate-on-delivery was rejected per AGENTS.md "Config/env surface bar is high" and the Codex review's explicit requirement "without adding a new config option or parallel message schema."

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **AI model**: glm-5.1
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Issue analysis, source code tracing across dynamic-tools.ts, embedded-agent-subscribe.ts, agent-loop.ts, and upstream Codex protocol (codex-rs/protocol/src/dynamic_tools.rs)

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest-risk area**: Duplicate channel messages after fix — if the generic-layer suppression (`suppressMessageToolOnlySourceReplyOutput`) does not correctly receive the `didDeliverSourceReplyViaMessageTool` flag, the agent could send both the intermediate message and the final output to the source channel.

**Mitigation**: The `didDeliverSourceReplyViaMessageTool` and `messagingToolSourceReplyPayloads` collection occurs before `withDynamicToolTermination` in the code path and is not gated by the `terminate` flag. The generic suppression layer checks `messagingToolSourceReplyPayloads.length > 0` to activate suppression, which remains correct. However, this needs verification via `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe*.test.ts` in a full build environment.

**Compatibility impact**: Backward compatible. No config/env changes. No new schema. The only behavior change is that intermediate source-reply messages no longer terminate the turn, which is the intended behavior per PR #92343.

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

target.body:
# PR5/5 - internal session delivery handoff + final hardening

## What Problem This Solves

This finishes the beta3 durable-core stack by turning resolved durable wake
obligations into an internal session delivery-queue handoff on gateway startup.
After PR4 made wakes inspectable and controllable, PR5 gives the durable runtime
a concrete recovery path: a resolved wake is replayed, persisted with delivery
evidence, and queued for the owning OpenClaw session without inventing external
channel sends.

## Stack position

- Stack item: PR5/5
- Clean PR5 comparison: `a30e2b6ce4e5f1390599380aedc82078c98854f7..443ffd2292e146fad3c089a03382a5f4702632f7`
- PR4 dependency: `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/105844`
- GitHub base rationale: existing PR1-PR4 stack PRs target `release/2026.7.1`; the PR4 branch exists on the fork, not as an upstream base branch, so this PR follows stack convention while documenting the exact PR4-head diff.

## Scope

- Adds `createDurableWakeSessionDeliveryHook`, which resolves durable wakes to
  agent/session keys and enqueues one internal `systemEvent` via the session
  delivery queue.
- Wires gateway startup durable wake replay through that hook.
- Persists delivery evidence with `internalDelivery: "session_delivery_queue"`
  and `noExternalSend: true`.
- Extends focused replay/startup tests for idempotency, startup replay, ambiguous
  target handling, and no autonomous resume/abandon/create-new policy.
- Updates durable docs to clarify the `delivered` state and CLI wake-attempt
  evidence.

## Non-scope

- No Discord, Signal, Slack, plugin, or other external transport delivery is
  implemented or claimed.
- No cron mutation.
- No release/changelog/package churn from the stale old PR5 ancestry.
- No broad durable orchestration policy changes beyond this internal handoff.

## Evidence

Clean scope:

```text
6 files changed, 372 insertions(+), 50 deletions(-)
```

Focused behavior:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/durable/wake-delivery-replay.test.ts src/durable/startup.test.ts
# pass: 2 files, 14 tests
```

Adjacent durable CLI/Gateway/read-path proof:

```bash

# pass: 3 Vitest shards, 4 files, 25 tests
```

Static/docs gates:

```bash

# pass

pnpm check:docs
# pass

git diff --check a30e2b6ce4e5f1390599380aedc82078c98854f7..HEAD
# pass
```

Remote proof attempts were made but unavailable in this shell:

```text
blacksmith-testbox: blocked, blacksmith CLI not found in PATH
aws Crabbox: blocked, broker login missing
```

## Upgrade contract

This PR adds no schema migration. It writes wake delivery attempts using the
existing durable wake attempt ledger and queues internal session deliveries using
the existing session delivery queue idempotency contract. Repeated startup replay
must not duplicate queued events once a wake is marked delivered.

## Risk / limits

- Main risk is semantic: reviewers should confirm `delivered` remains scoped to
  internal durable/session handoff and cannot be mistaken for external channel
  transport success.
- Remote Testbox proof is still desirable before merge because local provider
  setup blocked it here.
- Full release validation was not run for this narrow PR5 slice.

@clawsweeper review



### Live Gateway startup/restart proof at PR5 head

Additional live Gateway startup/restart proof at PR5 head `443ffd2292e146fad3c089a03382a5f4702632f7` was collected using a real local Gateway process twice against the same isolated state dir.

target.title: fix(gateway): evict oldest rate-limit bucket by window age, not insertion order
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`consumeControlPlaneWriteBudget()` uses `controlPlaneBuckets.keys().next().value` to pick a bucket to evict when the map reaches its 10,000-entry hard cap. The variable is named `oldest`.

`Map.keys().next()` returns the first key by **insertion order**, not the bucket with the **smallest `windowStartMs`** (i.e. the one whose rate-limit window is oldest by wall-clock time). These two orderings diverge because of how `Map.set()` interacts with the ECMAScript insertion-order guarantee:

- When `Map.set(existingKey, newValue)` is called for an **already-present** key, the value is updated but the key's insertion-order position is **left unchanged** (§23.1.3.9).
- Active buckets trigger `set()` during window resets (line 60), but they stay in their original insertion-order slot.
- Newer buckets inserted later can have genuinely older `windowStartMs` values while sitting behind the early-inserted but recently-reset active bucket.

This means an early-inserted, still-active bucket can be evicted while genuinely older (expired) buckets remain in the map. The active client's rate-limit state is lost, effectively giving it a free pass.

`pruneStaleControlPlaneBuckets()` (line 99–108) in the same file already uses the correct criterion — it walks the full map and tests each bucket's `windowStartMs`. The eviction path should use the same criterion.

## Why This Change Was Made

The eviction path now scans the full map for the bucket with the smallest `windowStartMs` instead of trusting insertion order. This matches the intent of the variable name `oldest` and aligns with `pruneStaleControlPlaneBuckets`.

The loop walks at most 10,000 entries (`CONTROL_PLANE_BUCKET_MAX_ENTRIES`), which takes < 1ms on a modern CPU. This path is cold: it only executes when a **new** client arrives while the map is already at its hard cap — a scenario that requires 10,000 unique device/IP combinations before it triggers even once. The cost is negligible and the path is identical every 1 in 10,000+ calls.

## User Impact

No user-observable API or config changes. The only affected scenario is a gateway under 10,000+ unique client identities — at which point eviction fairness improves: the bucket evicted is the one whose rate-limit window is actually oldest, not the one that was inserted first.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: `Map.keys().next()` (insertion order) used as a proxy for `min(windowStartMs)` (age order) in control-plane rate-limit bucket eviction. The two orders diverge per ECMAScript §23.1.3.9: `Map.set(existingKey, val)` does not reposition the key.

**The semantic gap in code** — before (left) vs after (right):

```
BEFORE (keys().next()):                         AFTER (min windowStartMs):
                                                 
Map.set() does not reposition existing keys.    Iterates all buckets to find the one whose
An active bucket that resets its window         windowStartMs is numerically smallest —
many times keeps its original insertion-        i.e. the bucket whose rate-limit window
order slot.                                     started earliest, and is therefore the
                                                 closest to expiry or already expired.
keys().next() → oldest by insertion, not age.   
                                                 old variable name "oldest" → now correct.

pruneStaleControlPlaneBuckets() already        pruneStaleControlPlaneBuckets() uses the
uses windowStartMs (line 101).  The eviction    same criterion — the two paths are aligned.
path diverged from this criterion.
```

**Proof that `Map.set(existingKey, _)` preserves insertion order** — ECMAScript specification §23.1.3.9 `Map.prototype.set`:

```
4. Let p be the Record {[[Key]]: key, [[Value]]: value}.
5. If p is not present, append p to the end of the List.
   (No repositioning step for existing keys.)
```

**Focus test verification**:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/control-plane-rate-limit.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/gateway/control-plane-rate-limit.ts
exit 0

$ git diff --stat HEAD~1..HEAD
 src/gateway/control-plane-rate-limit.ts | 18 ++++++++++++++----
 1 file changed, 14 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)
```

**Observed result**: All existing tests pass unchanged. The eviction path now selects the bucket with the smallest `windowStartMs` rather than the first key by insertion order.

**What was not tested**: A live gateway with 10,000+ unique device/IP identities exercising the eviction path. The pre-condition (10,000 unique clients) is a production extreme that is not practical to simulate in unit tests. The fix is verified through: (1) ECMAScript spec citation proving the old behavior was wrong, (2) alignment with the same file's own `pruneStaleControlPlaneBuckets` pattern, (3) existing tests still pass.

## Root Cause

In `consumeControlPlaneWriteBudget()`, the hard-cap eviction path used `controlPlaneBuckets.keys().next().value` as a proxy for "oldest bucket." The variable was named `oldest`, indicating the intent was age-based eviction.

`Map.keys().next()` returns keys by insertion order, not by `windowStartMs`. Per the ECMAScript specification (§23.1.3.9), `Map.set(key, value)` for an existing key updates the value but does **not** reposition the key in insertion order. An active bucket that resets its window via `set()` stays in its original insertion-order slot; a bucket inserted later can have an older `windowStartMs` while sitting behind it in insertion order.

The same file's `pruneStaleControlPlaneBuckets()` function already walks the full map and checks `bucket.windowStartMs` (line 101–102). The eviction path had inadvertently diverged from this criterion by using insertion order instead.

## AI Assistance

Analysis, root cause investigation, and this PR body were drafted with agent assistance. All commands were run locally.

target.title: fix: resolve Tavily SecretRefs in agent tools
target.body:
Fixes #95109

## Summary

- Select the active resolved runtime config snapshot in one shared helper before agent/plugin tool surfaces read credentials.
- Apply Tool Search defaults on top of that selected runtime config, so run-local overlays do not turn a resolved snapshot back into authored SecretRefs.
- Reuse the same selector from direct plugin-tool resolution and Tool Search resolution, avoiding drift between agent-visible plugin tools and direct plugin tools.
- Update Tavily's plugin-local API-key resolver to use inspect-mode SecretRef handling so a matching unresolved `env:*:TAVILY_API_KEY` ref can use the documented `process.env.TAVILY_API_KEY` fallback.
- Keep explicit non-env and nonmatching Tavily SecretRefs fail-closed instead of silently replacing file, exec, or other env refs with the ambient Tavily key.
- Add focused regressions for the agent Tool Search runtime snapshot path and the Tavily env fallback credential boundary.

## Root Cause

There were two related Tavily SecretRef failures at different ownership layers.

1. The agent Tool Search runtime-config overlay selected the wrong base config. The embedded attempt path and harness bridge applied local Tool Search defaults directly to `params.config`. When `params.config` was the authored source config, the overlay clone no longer matched the active runtime source snapshot, so later plugin-tool config selection treated it as explicit config and did not swap in the already-resolved runtime snapshot. Tavily then received an exec-backed SecretRef instead of the resolved in-memory string.
2. Tavily's plugin-local resolver used strict SecretRef normalization before the documented env fallback. `extensions/tavily/src/config.ts` called strict normalization on `plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey`; an unresolved env SecretRef threw before `process.env.TAVILY_API_KEY` could be read.

RCA proof:

- Agent Tool Search before behavior: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts` and `src/agents/harness/tool-surface-bridge.ts` applied Tool Search defaults before runtime snapshot selection.
- Existing selector proof: direct plugin tools already used the source/runtime snapshot matching rule; this PR moves that rule into `src/agents/tool-runtime-config.ts` and reuses it.
- Tavily before behavior: `extensions/tavily/src/config.ts` used strict SecretRef normalization ahead of the env fallback, which matches the `UnresolvedSecretInputError` in #95109.
- Dependency contract inspected: `resolveSecretInputString` strict mode throws on unresolved refs; inspect mode returns ref metadata so the plugin can allow only the matching env fallback and block file/exec/wrong-env refs.

## What Problem This Solves

Users with Tavily configured through resolved runtime SecretRefs can use agent-visible Tavily tools without the Tool Search overlay reintroducing unresolved source SecretRefs.

Users with Tavily configured as `{ source: "env", provider: "default", id: "TAVILY_API_KEY" }` can also rely on the documented gateway environment fallback when that env ref is not inline-resolved in the current read-only plugin path. Tavily still does not silently borrow `TAVILY_API_KEY` for file refs, exec refs, or env refs targeting another variable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The agent runtime now chooses the applicable resolved runtime snapshot before applying local Tool Search defaults. That keeps run-local config overlays in memory, preserves the authored SecretRef in source config, and avoids storing plaintext credentials.

The Tavily plugin now mirrors the inspect-mode SecretRef pattern used by sibling web providers: it classifies configured secrets as available, missing, or blocked before deciding whether the ambient env fallback is allowed.

## User Impact

Agent-visible Tavily tools can use exec/file/env SecretRefs that have already been resolved into the active runtime snapshot.

Tavily also no longer throws before checking `TAVILY_API_KEY` for the canonical env SecretRef configuration reported in #95109. Explicit non-env Tavily SecretRefs remain fail-closed if unavailable.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior fixed: Tool Search runtime config now carries resolved in-memory Tavily API key values to agent/plugin tools while the source config keeps the authored SecretRef; Tavily's plugin-local resolver now allows the matching env SecretRef fallback without weakening file/exec/wrong-env credential boundaries.

Closest feasible environment tested: focused Vitest coverage through the actual agent Tool Search runtime helpers and Tavily resolver code, plus current-head terminal proof through the real `tavily_search` tool entrypoint. The current-head proof configured Tavily with an env SecretRef, set only a generated dummy `TAVILY_API_KEY`, and called the real Tavily endpoint. Tavily returned the expected dummy-key auth failure instead of OpenClaw throwing `UnresolvedSecretInputError`.

Current-head Tavily env SecretRef proof:

```text
node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'SCRIPT'
# script imported createTavilySearchTool and resolveTavilyApiKey from this checkout
# cfg.plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey = { source: "env", provider: "default", id: "TAVILY_API_KEY" }
# process.env.TAVILY_API_KEY = generated dummy value only
SCRIPT

PR #97827 current-head Tavily env SecretRef proof
commit: 1b921e49532747c9031dc98096179f90fc3fb6b9
configured apiKey: env:default:TAVILY_API_KEY
endpoint: https://api.tavily.com/search
env key: generated dummy value only (redacted)
resolveTavilyApiKey returned env dummy: true
Tavily endpoint reached with dummy key: true
UnresolvedSecretInputError observed: no
observed error: Tavily Search API error (401): {"detail":{"error":"Unauthorized: missing or invalid API key."}}
```

Focused regression output:

```text

[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts
```

Observed after behavior:

- Agent Tool Search config keeps Tavily's resolved runtime string while the source config remains an authored SecretRef.
- Tavily resolves a matching unresolved `env:*:TAVILY_API_KEY` SecretRef from `process.env.TAVILY_API_KEY` instead of throwing first.
- The `tavily_search` tool path reaches Tavily with the resolved dummy env key and receives a Tavily auth error, proving provider execution was reached.

## Evidence

Autoreview:

## Verification

- Current-head real behavior proof: redacted dummy-key `tavily_search` call against `https://api.tavily.com/search` reached Tavily and returned 401 instead of `UnresolvedSecretInputError`.
- Focused regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/tavily/src/config.test.ts src/agents/harness/tool-surface-bridge.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.browser-plugin.integration.test.ts`

## What was not tested

- Live Tavily search with a real Tavily credential, to avoid exposing or storing a real API key. The current-head proof intentionally used a generated dummy key and treated Tavily's 401 response as proof that the provider endpoint was reached.
- A successful Tavily result payload with a real account quota.

target.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — core event contracts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
OpenClaw has operational diagnostics, OTEL exporters, and prompt-injection hardening, but no first-class AI safety/quality event taxonomy. Without a shared schema, safety signals (prompt injection attempts, tool policy decisions, external content ingestion, eval scores) are invisible to operators and cannot be correlated across sessions or exported consistently.

## Evidence
- `src/infra/diagnostic-events.ts` — `DiagnosticSecurityEvent.category` enum confirms no `ai_safety` category exists in main
- Clawsweeper review of issue #82548 (June 29) confirmed current main does not have the requested taxonomy
- New types: `ai_safety.prompt_injection.signal`, `ai_safety.tool_policy.decision`, `ai_safety.external_content.consumed`, `ai_safety.user_feedback.received`, `ai_safety.memory_context.selected`, `ai_safety.eval.result`
- 8 unit tests added in `src/infra/diagnostic-events.test.ts` covering each new event type and schema version constant
- Depends on: nothing (this is the unblocking schema PR)
- Unblocks: #107184 (exporters), #107187 (plugin API), #107192 (UI/CLI)

## Evidence — Clawsweeper re-review fixes (2026-07-14)

**Security fix:** `DiagnosticAISafetyEventPayload` is now excluded from `DiagnosticEventInput` (the untrusted `emitDiagnosticEvent()` surface). AI safety events are emittable only via the trusted core path (`emitTrustedDiagnosticEvent`, new `TrustedDiagnosticEventInput` type) or the policy-gated `emitPluginSafetyEvent` from #107187. A runtime gate mirroring the existing `security.event` gate additionally drops any `ai_safety.*` event emitted untrusted, so plugins cannot spoof safety findings even with an unsafe cast. Contract tests moved to `src/infra/diagnostic-ai-safety-events.test.ts` and now cover the untrusted-drop behavior:

```
✓ diagnostic AI safety events > exports AI_SAFETY_EVENT_SCHEMA_VERSION as numeric constant 1
✓ diagnostic AI safety events > drops AI safety events emitted through the untrusted emitDiagnosticEvent API
✓ diagnostic AI safety events > emits ai_safety.prompt_injection.signal with required fields via trusted path
✓ diagnostic AI safety events > emits ai_safety.prompt_injection.signal without optional fields
✓ diagnostic AI safety events > emits ai_safety.tool_policy.decision with all fields
✓ diagnostic AI safety events > emits ai_safety.external_content.consumed with hashed URL only
✓ diagnostic AI safety events > emits ai_safety.user_feedback.received with normalized score
✓ diagnostic AI safety events > emits ai_safety.memory_context.selected with item count and tokens
✓ diagnostic AI safety events > emits ai_safety.eval.result with pass/fail and score
✓ diagnostic AI safety events > all six AI safety event types carry standard seq/ts enrichment

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  10 passed (10)
```

**4-PR series design note:** the security boundary is deliberate across the stack — this PR defines the contracts and locks the untrusted path; #107184 wires exporters and preserves emitter provenance; #107187 adds the only plugin-facing emission surface, gated by manifest `safetyEventTypes`; #107192 adds observability surfaces. Untrusted path gated, trusted path only.

**OTEL note:** full end-to-end OTEL integration proof requires a running collector, which is not available in CI; exporter behavior is covered by unit tests in #107184.

### Live simulation output
<details>
<summary>Terminal output — emitting all 6 event types through trusted path (re-run 2026-07-14 after rebase onto upstream/main)</summary>

target.title: fix(codex): bound app-server websocket handshake waits at 30s
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using Codex app-server over `websocket`/`unix` transport would hang forever on `initialize`/RPC when a peer accepted TCP but never completed the WebSocket upgrade. Pending frames never flush and the client never sees a transport exit, so the run cannot fail closed or reconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add a private `buildCodexAppServerWebSocketOptions` that sets `handshakeTimeout: 30_000` (same floor as Slack relay / Mattermost / Discord gateway).
- Both TCP and Unix upgrade paths consume that builder.
- Guard `EventEmitter` error re-emit with `listenerCount` so callers that only wait on `exit` (handshake hang paths) are not disrupted by Node's unhandled-`error` throw.
- Add `testHooks` for test-only short handshake floors; production omits them and uses the 30s default.

Collision check: searched open PRs for "codex websocket handshake timeout app-server"; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found.

## User Impact

- **Before**: A peer that accepts TCP but never completes the WS upgrade hangs `CodexAppServerClient.initialize()` and all subsequent RPC calls forever — no timeout, no error, no reconnect.
- **After**: Handshake times out after 30s with a `close` event and error, allowing the client to fail closed or retry. Working WebSocket connections are unaffected.

## Verification

- Exact head: `6c71011`
- `oxfmt --check extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts proof-codex-ws-handshake.mts` — passed.
- `oxlint <same files>` — passed; exit 0.
- `git diff --check` — passed; exit 0.
- Focused tests:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-websocket.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```

 ✓ can speak JSON-RPC over the canonical unix control socket 14ms
 ✓ uses a 30s handshakeTimeout matching Slack relay / Mattermost 3ms
 ✓ negative control: ws without handshakeTimeout stays CONNECTING on never-upgrade peer 307ms
 ✓ emits exit when the websocket handshake never completes 205ms
 ✓ fails initialize when the websocket handshake never completes 206ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
```

- Standalone production-path proof (9 structured assertions):

```bash
node --import tsx proof-codex-ws-handshake.mts
```

```

head=6c710118d0c766c98543928c8fd20b21061f7d51
[case 1] negative control — ws without handshakeTimeout stays CONNECTING
  ok: without handshakeTimeout, stays CONNECTING after 300ms
  ok: readyState is CONNECTING
  info: outcome=still-pending readyState=CONNECTING wait_ms=300

[case 2] positive control — createWebSocketTransport times out
  ok: production handshake timeout is 30s
  ok: transport killed after timeout
  ok: exit code is 1006 (abnormal closure)
  ok: resolved in under 2s (not 30s production floor)
  ok: resolved after the proof timeout
  info: killed=true exit_code=1006 elapsed_ms=201 proof_timeout_ms=200 production_timeout_ms=30000

[case 3] valid server — client communicates over real WebSocket
```
